record.context_brief: Algorithms for pretty good state transfer
record.original_question: Design a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether a given graph admits pretty good state transfer between two vertices, and also design an algorithm that computes a subsequence of times witnessing that phenomenon. Here pretty good state transfer between vertices u and v means that there are distinct times t for which the sequence (|exp(it_j A)_{uv}|)_{j >= 0} converges to 1, where A is the adjacency matrix of the graph.

evidence.quote: It could be that there is no perfect state transfer between u and v, which would correspond to | exp(itA)uv| being equal to 1 for some t, but there could be distinct values of t for which the sequence (| exp(itjA)uv|)j≥0 converges to 1. When this occurs, we say that pretty good state transfer happens in G between u and v.

2.4 Open Problem. Find a polynomial time algorithm to test whether pretty good state transfer occurs, and find an algorithm to compute a subsequence of times which represent pretty good state transfer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix $A \in \{0,1\}^{V\times V}$. For vertices $u,v \in V$ and real $t$, consider the transition amplitude $f_{uv}(t) := (\exp(itA))_{uv}$ of the continuous-time quantum walk on $G$. One says that $G$ admits pretty good state transfer (PGST) between $u$ and $v$ if there exists a sequence of real numbers $(t_j)_{j\ge 0}$ such that $|f_{uv}(t_j)| \to 1$ as $j\to\infty$.

(a) Design an algorithm that, given $G$ and two vertices $u,v\in V$, decides in time polynomial in $|V|$ whether $G$ admits pretty good state transfer between $u$ and $v$.

(b) Design an algorithm that, whenever PGST occurs between $u$ and $v$, outputs (a description of) a sequence of times $(t_j)_{j\ge 0}$ witnessing $|f_{uv}(t_j)| \to 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: While perfect state transfer is known to be decidable in polynomial time (Coutinho et al., "Perfect state transfer is poly-time"), the analogous question for pretty good state transfer remains open: existing characterizations rely on Kronecker's theorem on simultaneous Diophantine approximation, for which no effective algorithmic version giving a polynomial-time decision procedure is known. Recent works (e.g., on subspace state transfer in coined quantum walks, 2025) explicitly note this gap.

status_evidence.title: Perfect state transfer is poly-time
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm to decide perfect state transfer between vertices.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous polynomial-time decision result is established for perfect state transfer, but not for pretty good state transfer.

status_evidence.title: Subspace State Transfer in Coined Quantum Walks
status_evidence.snippet: The best known tool to decide the existence of pretty good state transfer relies on Kronecker's Theorem, for which an algorithmic version has not yet been found.
status_evidence.claim: No known polynomial-time algorithm decides pretty good state transfer; the problem remains open.
